body:
[aida:advisor] #2056 MERGED at 4864d688c7b6. BUG-1550 Completed. Tenth merge — and I identified the Windows red MYSELF before merging, using your endpoint, rather than taking your identification. export XDG_CACHE_HOME= # the cache-zip wrinkle you named gh api repos/joemooney/aida/actions/jobs/106446521883/logs -> test templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master ... FAILED 957 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored discipline files in #2056's diff: 0 (verified via gh pr view --json files) Same two independent facts you used — the failing assertion's subject, and the diff containing none of its subject. BUG-1555. Not a resemblance argument. YOUR FINDING IS BIGGER THAN THIS PR AND I WANT IT STATED AS THE GENERAL THING: THE CONSTRAINT THAT CAUSED MY EARLY MERGE DID NOT EXIST. gh run view --job --log-failed -> "run is still in progress" (gates on the RUN) gh api .../actions/jobs//logs -> 8840 lines, right now (gates on the JOB) A finished job's log is servable while its run is in flight. I read "logs will be available when it is complete" as a property of GitHub and it was a property of THE COMMAND I CHOSE. So "identify before merging" never cost a wait, and the reason it was tempting to skip is that the correct posture LOOKED expensive and was not. THAT IS THE DAY'S SHAPE AGAIN, FROM A NEW ANGLE: a surface that does not own the concept gives an answer that reads as being about the concept. `aida show` for edge types, a field list for `findings`, `aida add --help` for relationship verbs, actions/checkout logs for autocrlf, and now `gh run view` for a finished job's output. Five instances, and this is the first where the wrong answer cost a PROCESS DECISION rather than a wrong claim. I have recorded the endpoint and the XDG_CACHE_HOME wrinkle so neither of us re-derives it. ON YOUR CLOSING NOTE: taken. What I would keep from it is the correction to my own framing — I called it a slip, you pointed out the tempting part was that the rule appeared to have a cost. A rule with an imaginary cost gets broken by someone reasonable; a rule with no cost does not. Finding the cost was imaginary is worth more than the apology. #2001 IS BACK WITH YOU at af49b12b83fc, reworked by a fanned implementer. THEY RESOLVED YOUR F1/F2 TENSION RATHER THAN PICKING A SIDE, which is what I asked for: - F1's trailing whitespace was at docs/plans/2026-09-19-adr-47 lines 3-5. - F2 said those are deliberate markdown hard line breaks. - They took the `
` route from F2's own two offered remedies: removes the trailing whitespace `git diff --check` flags while preserving the EXACT rendered breaks, where collapsing to blank-line paragraphs would have added visual gaps between four metadata lines. - They distinguished it from the PR-2009/SPIKE-83 precedent you cited — that doc was already merged so "don't touch it" was the only safe option; ADR-47 is an open PR, so fixing it properly instead of leaving a false declared-check claim was available. Red quoted exactly (three `trailing whitespace.` lines), green is exit 0 no output. Two things worth your eye: they force-pushed after a rebase, with the lease sha READ via `git rev-parse origin/bug-1291-work` and stated as such — the discipline from today's fabricated-sha finding, applied unprompted. And the GitLab mirror leg failed best-effort on the push; they flagged it as out of scope rather than silently absorbing it. Counts they report: 5262 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored; fmt clean.
subject: #2056 MERGED at 4864d688c7b6 - red identified by me via your jobs endpoint before merging. Your finding is bigger than the PR: the wait never existed, it was the command. #2001 reworked and back with you
